# TranscriptomicsHW: DE analysis

1 and 8 -\> Lung and Blood Vessels

```{r}
library(recount3)
library(edgeR)
library(ggplot2)
rse_brain <- readRDS("rse_brain.RDS")
rse_blood <- readRDS("rse_blood.RDS")
rse_lung <- readRDS("rse_lung.RDS")
assays(rse_brain)$counts <- transform_counts(rse_brain)
assays(rse_blood)$counts <- transform_counts(rse_blood)
assays(rse_lung)$counts <- transform_counts(rse_lung)
```

## Building the counting table

```{r}
x <- cbind(counts_brain_selected,counts_blood_selected,counts_lung_selected)

colnames(x) <- c("Brain69", "Brain70","Brain73", "Blood70","Blood71","Blood72","Lung69","Lung71","Lung72")

rownames(x) <- rowData(rse_brain_selected)$gene_name

y <- DGEList(counts=x)
```

```{r}
group <- as.factor(c("Brain","Brain","Brain","Blood","Blood","Blood","Lung","Lung","Lung"))

y$samples$group <- group

y
```
y and group are important to put up the linear model

```{r}
y$samples$rin <- as.factor(c(colData(rse_brain_selected)$gtex.smrin,colData(rse_blood_selected)$gtex.smrin,colData(rse_lung_selected)$gtex.smrin))
 
y$samples$slice <- as.factor(c(colData(rse_brain_selected)$gtex.smtsd,colData(rse_blood_selected)$gtex.smtsd,colData(rse_lung_selected)$gtex.smtsd))

y$samples$sex <- as.factor(c(colData(rse_brain_selected)$gtex.sex,colData(rse_blood_selected)$gtex.sex,colData(rse_lung_selected)$gtex.sex))

y$samples$mapped <- as.factor(c(colData(rse_brain_selected)$"recount_qc.star.uniquely_mapped_reads_%_both", colData(rse_blood_selected)$"recount_qc.star.uniquely_mapped_reads_%_both",colData(rse_lung_selected)$"recount_qc.star.uniquely_mapped_reads_%_both"))
```

boxplot after normalization
```{r}
boxplot(logcpm_after, notch=T, las=2)
```


```{r}

library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(tibble)

# 1. Convert matrix to a tidy data frame
# We turn the matrix into a tibble, then pivot it to long format
df_long <- as.data.frame(logcpm_before) %>%
  rownames_to_column(var = "gene") %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -gene, names_to = "sample", values_to = "expression")

# 2. Add the group information from your 'y' object
# We map the sample names to their corresponding groups
df_long$group <- y$samples$group[match(df_long$sample, rownames(y$samples))]

# 3. Define your colors
my_colors <- c("Brain" = "forestgreen", "Blood" = "darkred", "Lung" = "darkblue")

# 4. Create the beautiful ggplot
p1<- ggplot(df_long, aes(x = sample, y = expression, fill = group)) +
  geom_boxplot(notch = TRUE, alpha = 0.8, outlier.size = 0.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = my_colors) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  labs(title = "Log-CPM Values before normalization",
       x = "Sample", 
       y = "Log-CPM") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        legend.position = "top")

# 1. Convert matrix to a tidy data frame
# We turn the matrix into a tibble, then pivot it to long format
df_long1 <- as.data.frame(logcpm_after) %>%
  rownames_to_column(var = "gene") %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -gene, names_to = "sample", values_to = "expression")

# 2. Add the group information from your 'y' object
# We map the sample names to their corresponding groups
df_long1$group <- y$samples$group[match(df_long$sample, rownames(y$samples))]

# 4. Create the beautiful ggplot
p2 <- ggplot(df_long1, aes(x = sample, y = expression, fill = group)) +
  geom_boxplot(notch = TRUE, alpha = 0.8, outlier.size = 0.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = my_colors) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  labs(title = "Log-CPM Values after normalization",
       x = "Sample", 
       y = "Log-CPM") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        legend.position = "top")

p1

p2
```

### I plot my samples in a 2d space
Observe the Two dimensional Plot! If something is far it may be due to technical, reads, or also biological reasons aka mithocondria stuff
```{r}

logcpm

# Ensure the order matches the levels of y$samples$group

sample_colors

# 2. Plot using the col argument

plotMDS(logcpm, col = sample_colors, main="MDS plot of Brain, Blood and Lung Samples (logCPM)") +
```

when a replicate is far form the cluster, after expression profile and normalization:

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(ggrepel)
library(ggforce)
library(limma)

# 1. Get the MDS coordinates
mds <- plotMDS(logcpm, plot = FALSE)
df_mds <- data.frame(
  Dim1 = mds$x,
  Dim2 = mds$y,
  Sample = colnames(logcpm),
  Group = y$samples$group
)

# 2. Define your cute color palette
# Using softer, more aesthetic tones
cute_colors <- c("Brain" = "#FFA07A", "Blood" = "#8B0000", "Lung" = "#FFB6C1")

# 3. Create the ggplot
ggplot(df_mds, aes(x = Dim1, y = Dim2, color = Group)) +
  # Add the points
  geom_point(size = 4, alpha = 0.8) +
  # Use ggrepel to label points without overlap
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = Sample), size = 3, color = "black") +
  # Use your custom aesthetic colors
  scale_color_manual(values = cute_colors) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cute_colors) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  labs(title = "MDS Clustering by Tissue",
       subtitle = "Visualizing biological similarity",
       x = paste0("Dimension 1 (", round(mds$var.explained[1]*100), "%)"),
       y = paste0("Dimension 2 (", round(mds$var.explained[2]*100), "%)")) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```
```{r}
df_mds_meta <- cbind(df_mds, y$samples)
```

## Differential Expression Analysis
```{r}
fit <- glmQLFit(y, design)
fit
```

## Comparisons

###Blood-Brain

```{r}
qlfBlBr <- glmQLFTest(fit, contrast=c(-1,1,0))

qlfBlBr
```

###Blood-Lung

```{r}
qlfBlL <- glmQLFTest(fit, contrast=c(-1,0,1))

qlfBlL
```

###Brain-Lung

```{r}
qlfBrL <- glmQLFTest(fit, contrast=c(0,-1,1))

qlfBrL
```

```{r}
head(qlfBlBr$table)
```

```{r}
topTags(qlfBlBr, n=10,adjust.method = "BH", sort.by = "PValue")
```
```{r}
topTags(qlfBlL, n=10,adjust.method = "BH", sort.by = "PValue")
```
```{r}
topTags(qlfBrL, n=10,adjust.method = "BH", sort.by = "PValue")
```
I have log2FC:
- depends on the contrast. 
- negative logFC means that the first has a higher expression than the second


TO HAVE ALL OF THE RESULTS, the entire table and save it to excel

## 1v2 the true challenge
```{r}
res1 = decideTests(qlfBlBr) # (Blood vs Brain)
res2 = decideTests(qlfBlL) # (Blood vs Lung)
res3 = decideTests(qlfBrL) # (Brain vs Lung)
brain_specific <- rownames(res1)[res1[,1] == -1 & res3[,1] == 1]

colnames(design)

qlfBl <- glmQLFTest(fit, contrast = c(1,-0.5,-0.5))
qlfBr <- glmQLFTest(fit, contrast = c(-0.5,1,-0.5))
qlfL <- glmQLFTest(fit, contrast = c(-0.5,-0.5,1))


topTags(qlfBl, n=10,adjust.method = "BH", sort.by = "PValue")
topTags(qlfBr, n=10,adjust.method = "BH", sort.by = "PValue")
topTags(qlfL, n=10,adjust.method = "BH", sort.by = "PValue")

top100br <- topTags(qlfBr, n=100,adjust.method = "BH", sort.by = "PValue")
top100bl <- topTags(qlfBl, n=100,adjust.method = "BH", sort.by = "PValue")
top100l<- topTags(qlfL, n=100,adjust.method = "BH", sort.by = "PValue")

cat(rownames(top100br), sep = "\n")
cat(rownames(top100bl), sep = "\n")
cat(rownames(top100l), sep = "\n")

summary(decideTests(qlfBr, p.value=0.05, adjust.method = "BH", lfc = 1))
summary(decideTests(qlfBl, p.value=0.05, adjust.method = "BH", lfc = 1))
summary(decideTests(qlfL, p.value=0.05, adjust.method = "BH", lfc = 1))

```

```{r}
library(edgeR)

# 1. Get the top 1000 genes for each comparison (to ensure we have enough to find intersections)
# We take 1000 to be safe, then intersect, then sort by p-value
top_BlBr <- topTags(qlfBlBr, n = 1000)$table
top_BlLu <- topTags(qlfBlL, n = 1000)$table
top_BrLu <- topTags(qlfBrL, n = 1000)$table

# 2. Define the intersection logic (using the row names)
# Blood: Up in Bl vs Br (logFC > 0) AND Up in Bl vs Lu (logFC > 0)
blood_genes <- intersect(rownames(top_BlBr[top_BlBr$logFC > 0,]), 
                         rownames(top_BlLu[top_BlLu$logFC > 0,]))

# Brain: Down in Bl vs Br (logFC < 0) AND Up in Br vs Lu (logFC > 0)
brain_genes <- intersect(rownames(top_BlBr[top_BlBr$logFC < 0,]), 
                         rownames(top_BrLu[top_BrLu$logFC > 0,]))

# Lung: Down in Bl vs Lu (logFC < 0) AND Down in Br vs Lu (logFC < 0)
lung_genes <- intersect(rownames(top_BlLu[top_BlLu$logFC < 0,]), 
                        rownames(top_BrLu[top_BrLu$logFC < 0,]))

# 3. Get the top 100 and sort by PValue
# Here we take the intersection and sort them by the p-value from one of the tests
get_top100_ordered <- function(genes, ref_table) {
  subset_table <- ref_table[rownames(ref_table) %in% genes, ]
  subset_table <- subset_table[order(subset_table$PValue), ]
  return(head(rownames(subset_table), 100))
}

final_blood <- get_top100_ordered(blood_genes, top_BlBr)
final_brain <- get_top100_ordered(brain_genes, top_BrLu)
final_lung  <- get_top100_ordered(lung_genes, top_BlLu)

# 4. Print for Enrichr
cat("BLOOD:\n", final_blood, sep = "\n")
cat("\nBRAIN:\n", final_brain, sep = "\n")
cat("\nLUNG:\n", final_lung, sep = "\n")
```

## Check if DEG are DE in entire dataset
I first convert into TPM


```{r}
library(recount)
assays(rse_brain)$TPM <- recount::getTPM(rse_brain)
assays(rse_blood)$TPM <- recount::getTPM(rse_blood)
assays(rse_lung)$TPM <- recount::getTPM(rse_lung)
which(rowData(rse_brain)$gene_name == "CEACAM6")
which(rowData(rse_brain)$gene_name == "INA")
which(rowData(rse_brain)$gene_name == "CTSE")
which(rowData(rse_blood)$gene_name == "ACTA1")

plotCounts(y, gene = 10396, intgroup = "group", 
           main = "ACTA1 Expression Check")
```
